title: The Terracotta Army
passages: More than two thousand years ago, a ruler named Qin Shi Huang became the first emperor of a united China in 221 BC. He hoped to stay powerful even after death, so he ordered a huge army made of baked clay called TERRACOTTA. Thousands of workers spent many years shaping soldiers, horses and CHARIOTS to guard his tomb. The emperor died in about 210 BC, and his clay army was buried in great pits near the city now called Xi'an. Each soldier was made about the height of a real person, and craftsmen gave them different hairstyles, clothing and armor.

For more than two thousand years, the army lay hidden underground. Then, in March 1974, farmers digging a well struck pieces of a clay figure. ARCHAEOLOGISTS soon arrived and uncovered pit after pit. Experts now think there are more than 8,000 soldiers, along with about 130 chariots and over 600 horses. Many have still not been dug up. Some figures once wore bright paint, but most of the color faded soon after it met the air. Today, millions of visitors travel to see these silent guards, each with its own INDIVIDUAL face, and wonder what daily life was like in ancient China.
